summary.description: A thick, colourless, volatile liquid with a sweet odour. It is a volatile organic compound (VOC) mainly used as a degreasing agent and solvent.
emission_sources: Industrial use as a metal degreasing agent
Use in paints, lubricants, and paint strippers
environmental_impact: High exposure can cause neurological symptoms, irregular heartbeat, and possibly cancer
Contributes to ground-level ozone formation, which affects human health and plants
Does not bioaccumulate but persists in soil and evaporates quickly from water

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: High exposure to trichloroethylene is associated with serious health risks including neurological effects and potential carcinogenicity, and contributes to ozone formation that impacts respiratory health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Trichloroethylene’s persistence in soil and risks during use and disposal highlight the need for safer industrial practices and sustainable chemical management.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: As a VOC that contributes to ground-level ozone and persists in urban soils, trichloroethylene affects the environmental health of communities and urban ecosystems.
